title: Episode-driven canary orchestrator and rate-cap fallback
author: Elena Torres
release_notes: Introduce an episode-driven canary orchestrator that groups short-lived traffic episodes for more stable statistical comparisons; add a rate-cap fallback to avoid overload during spiky cutovers. Backwards compatible; configurable via canary policy flags.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see noisy short traffic bursts during canary evaluations that inflate variance and cause spurious rollback decisions. Previous guard logic operated on fixed windows which either missed regressions in low-traffic periods or overreacted to transient spikes. This PR implements an episode-driven orchestration layer which: 1) identifies contiguous "episodes" of traffic based on request inter-arrival time and per-route signal consistency; 2) aggregates statistics inside episodes for robust percentile estimates; and 3) applies a rate-cap-based fallback when episode-based routing would otherwise increase upstream concurrency beyond safe thresholds.

Design summary: The new EpisodeOrchestrator component lives in perf-canary/orchestrator and integrates with the existing probe scheduler. Episodes are detected by a lightweight state machine (idle -> collecting -> quiesce) using a tunable inter-arrival threshold and minimum episode size. Statistical aggregation supports weighted quantile merging so short episodes do not dominate long ones. The rate-cap fallback is a conservative gate: when projected cutover QPS would exceed configured rate caps for the target pool, traffic is throttled and progressively ramped using a token-bucket-like controller with backoff.

What this PR changes: Adds orchestrator core, exposes policy knobs in canary policy schema, updates the probe scheduler to request episode boundaries (so probes can be correlated to episodes), extends the evaluation engine to compute episode-aware baselines, and wireframes a simple dashboard tile in the Console for episode health and projected cutover QPS. Includes unit tests, integration test scenarios, and a small synthetic load harness used in local verification.

Checklist:
- [x] Episode detection algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Weighted-merge quantile estimator added
- [x] Rate-cap fallback controller implemented with canary policy override
- [x] Integration tests covering: low-traffic, bursty-traffic, and sustained load cutover
- [x] Console tile and metrics exported (episode_count, episode_duration_p95, projected_cutover_qps)
- [x] Documentation page added to perf-canary/docs describing policy knobs and recommended defaults

Testing and validation: Local synthetic runs using the attached harness demonstrated reduced false-positive rollback events in the bursty-traffic scenario (historical test set: false positives reduced from 6/10 to 1/10). Integration test suite includes a seeded seed-traffic generator and deterministic randomization so CI can reproduce episodes. CI initially flagged a flaky integration that depended on real-time timers; I replaced timer sleeps with a virtual clock in tests which resolved flakiness.

Operational considerations and rollout plan: The feature is behind a canary policy feature flag (episode_orchestrator: enabled=false by default). We will roll out to canary namespace batches: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with the rate-cap fallback enabled for the first two phases to avoid unexpected concurrency increases. We recommend enabling on low-traffic routes first and monitoring the new episode metrics for at least 48 hours.

Related work: builds on probe correlation hooks added in ENG-1443 and complements the traffic curation probe work. Linear tickets: ENG-1895 (feature), ENG-1950 (dashboard).

merge: Merged by Arjun Patel via squash on 2026-02-18. Commit message consolidated to 'episode-driven canary orchestrator + rate-cap fallback; documentation and tests.'
notes_on_risk: Low-medium. The algorithm is conservative by default and requires explicit policy opt-in. Highest risk is misconfiguration leading to overly aggressive throttling; mitigated by observability and gradual rollout. No infra migrations or DB schema changes.
testing_summary: Unit coverage added for episode state transitions and quantile merger. Integration scenarios cover three canonical traffic shapes. Local harness reproducibly reproduces historical noisy-burst traces used by the SRE playbook.
rollback_plan: Feature behind flag: disable episode_orchestrator in canary policy and the system will revert to previous fixed-window canary logic. If rate-cap fallback causes excessive throttling, set rate_cap.max_qps to previous baseline and remove progressive ramp. Ops runbook added under perf-canary/docs/runbooks/episode_orchestrator_rollout.md
